question.text: A default by a member in the derivatives segment is treated as:

answer.text: A default in ALL segments of that exchange and as a default on ALL exchanges where the member holds membership
A default only in the derivatives segment of that particular exchange
A default only across exchanges but limited to the derivatives segment
An isolated event with no impact on other segments or exchanges

explanation.text: The Logic: A default by a member in the derivatives segment is treated as a default in all segments of that exchange and as a default on all exchanges where the member holds membership. This cross-segment and cross-exchange treatment ensures that a defaulting member cannot continue operations elsewhere through the same membership. The Trap: The default treatment is not isolated to the derivatives segment or to one exchange. Once a default occurs in derivatives, the consequences flow across every segment of that exchange and across every other exchange where the member is registered. Note: Source basis is p.178 of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives Certification Examination workbook (December 2025 v1).
